sections.sectionSummaryBrief: There is another interpretation of "shevi" as return from exile, indicating a higher level than those needing redemption, and this distinction is explored.

translations.translation: And behold, there is another interpretation of "shevi,"
that "shevi" is from the term "return,"
the return from exile.
For the term "return"
[and particularly when it is in conjunction with the word "tifadeh" preceding it]
indicates that even before the return, he is not in exile,
but rather he is located in another place
(the place of exile)
and needs to go back and return to his place.
Accordingly, "shevi" are more elevated than those about whom "tifadeh" is said.
For the term "pidyon" (redemption) applies to one who is in exile,
(unlike this, where he is merely located in the place of exile)
and needs to be redeemed from exile.
And it needs to be understood,
how is it possible that the redemption of those who are in exile is through judgment
(according to the line of law),
and the return of those who are merely located in the place of exile
(who are more elevated)
is through charity.
And also it needs to be understood,
who are the two types concerning whom "tifadeh" and "shevi" are said.
For "tifadeh" is said regarding Tzion, which refers
(as above)
to Israel who engage in Torah and mitzvos,
and nevertheless they are in exile and need redemption,
and what is the merit of those called "shevi" who are not in exile.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Exile and captivity apply only to vessels, not to light, as light inherently dispels darkness.

translations.translation: And it will be understood by prefacing what is explained in the maamar,
that the matter of exile and captivity applies specifically to vessels,
because they are in the category of existence of a thing,
unlike the light,
which is in the category of nothingness,
exile does not apply to it.
And this matter
(that exile does not apply to light)
is also understood simply.
For a little light dispels much darkness,
meaning that even after the descent and drawing down of light into measurement and limitation
[for then specifically it is possible to say a little or a lot],
even then it dispels the darkness,
to the extent that even a little light dispels much darkness.
And furthermore,
darkness is automatically dispelled before light.
[For at the beginning of creation, light and darkness were intermingled,
but after "God separated between the light and between the darkness,"
darkness is dispelled before light.]
And from this it is also understood simply,
that in light, the matter of exile does not apply,
for darkness
(of exile)
is dispelled before light.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Similarly, the soul is like light and is not in exile, only the body is, yet the soul needs to be returned because it is clothed in the body.

translations.translation: And behold, the same applies to soul and body,
which are analogous to light and vessel.
As is known from the statement of my father-in-law, the Rebbe,
that only the body is in exile, not the soul.
That is,
even though the soul is clothed in the body and the body is in exile,
nevertheless, regarding the soul, this is not a matter of exile.
But only that because the body is in exile,
the soul that is clothed in it is located not in its place and needs return.
And as our sages said,
"I am asleep in exile, but my heart is awake,"
that even when "I am asleep in exile,"
the soul
(and my heart)
is awake.
For since the soul is literally a part of G-d above,
that even when it is in the manner of "mamash" (actual), from the term "mamashus" (materiality),
meaning it is clothed in a physical body,
it is a part of G-d above
[to the extent that it is literally a part of G-d above],
and it is known the statement of the Baal Shem Tov,
that when you grasp a part of the essence, you grasp all of it,
therefore,
even after its descent and clothing in the body with the power that separates,
and even during the time of exile,
it is not in exile, etc.
And accordingly, it can be said,
that the term "shevi" refers not only to a special type among Israel,
but also to the soul of each and every Jew.
For since the soul is not in exile,
the term "pidyon" (redemption) does not apply to it.
But nevertheless, it needs return,
for since the soul is clothed in the body,
to the extent that it is affected by the events of the body,
through the exile of the body,
the soul is also located in the place of exile,
and therefore needs return.
